title: Clock Decomposition Explorer
creator: Dan McCreary
subject: Clocks and Watches with AI
description: Explore a tree that breaks a digital clock into five sub-problems and thirteen small tasks, then pick a bug symptom and see which task is the most likely suspect.

educational.topic: Decomposition: breaking a digital clock into sub-problems
learningObjectives: Analyze a digital clock by breaking it into sub-problems and smaller tasks.
Identify which sub-problem a given symptom most likely belongs to.
Describe how to test one small piece of a program by itself.
prerequisites: Read the Decomposition section of Chapter 1.

accessibility.notes: Screen-reader description provided; all controls are standard HTML elements.

controls.label: Tree boxes
controls.description: Clicking a box shows its job and a "Test it alone" hint.

controls.label: Tree boxes
controls.description: Hovering highlights the path back to the root.

controls.label: Symptom
controls.description: Pulses the task most likely to contain the bug and explains why.

controls.label: Navigation buttons
controls.description: Pan and zoom the tree without capturing page scrolling.

keyQuestions: Why does the "wrong hour" bug point to Format Time and not Keep Time?
Which small task would you test first if the display is completely blank?
Why is it easier to test "Compute minutes" alone than the whole clock?
commonMisconceptions: Starting the search at the top of the program instead of at the piece closest to the symptom.
Assuming a display problem must be in Draw Time, when the display may be drawing exactly what Format Time told it to.
Thinking decomposition is only for planning. It is just as useful for finding bugs.
assessmentOpportunities: Given a symptom, students name the sub-problem and the small task most likely to contain the bug.
Students explain why the other sub-problems can be ruled out for that symptom.
Students write a test that checks one small task by itself.
